after.problem: A point $P$ has Cartesian coordinates $(-8,-15).$ What are the polar coordinates of $P?$ Round your answer to two decimal places where necessary.
after.worked_solution:
First, we determine $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-8)^{2}+(-15)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{64+225} \\  & =\sqrt{289} \\  & =17\end{aligned}
$$

For the reference angle, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\theta }_{R} & =|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{-15}{-8})| \\  & ≈1.080\,84.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the point $P$ lies in the third quadrant, we add the reference angle to $\pi ,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta  & =\pi +{\theta }_{R} \\  & =\pi +1.080\,84 \\  & ≈4.22,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to two decimal places. Therefore, the polar coordinates of $P$ are  $(17,4.22).$

after.problem: A point $P$ has Cartesian coordinates $(5,0).$ What are the polar coordinates of $P?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we determine $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{5}^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Since the point $P$ lies on the positive half of the $x$-axis, we have $\theta =0.$ 

Therefore, the polar coordinates of $P$ are $(5,0).$

after.problem: A point $P$ has Cartesian coordinates $(-k,k),$ where $k$ is a positive real number. What are the polar coordinates of $P?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we determine $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-k)^{2}+{k}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2{k}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

For the reference angle, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\theta }_{R} & =|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{-k}{k})| \\  & =|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(-1)| \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the point $P$ lies in the second quadrant, we subtract the reference angle from $\pi $ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta  & =\pi -{\theta }_{R} \\  & =\pi -\frac{\pi }{4} \\  & =\frac{3\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}

content.problem: A point $P$ has Cartesian coordinates $(-k,k),$ where $k$ is a positive real number. What are the polar coordinates of $P?$
content.worked_solution:
First, we determine $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-k)^{2}+{k}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2{k}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

For the reference angle, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\theta }_{R} & =|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{-k}{k})| \\  & =|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(-1)| \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the point $P$ lies in the second quadrant, we subtract the reference angle from $\pi $ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta  & =\pi -{\theta }_{R} \\  & =\pi -\frac{\pi }{4} \\  & =\frac{3\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the polar coordinates of $P$ are $(\sqrt{2}\,k,\frac{3\pi }{4}).$
